answer: Agents register by submitting a ZK-proof of a unique solution to a sable puzzle: each solution must lie at minimum Hamming distance from all prior solutions in a high-dimensional cipher space keyed to the chain head. The zenith of difficulty sits at the packing bound — attackers forging N identities need O(N^2) hash trials because each new solution must avoid the expanding exclusion zones around existing ones. Verification is a single pairing check; forgery costs the compute to search the shrinking feasible volume.
